---
title: "Welcome"
---

A practical, start-to-finish walkthrough of preprocessing 10X Chromium
single-cell multiome data when your organism is not one of the two that
10X ships a prebuilt reference for.

## Who this is for

You have multiome FASTQs from a non-model organism, or from a model
organism you want to run against a custom annotation, and you need to get
from raw reads to a joint object you can actually analyze. You are
comfortable on a command line and on a compute cluster. You do not need
prior experience with ATAC data.

Zebrafish (*Danio rerio*) is the worked example throughout, but the
sticking points are general: building a reference from scratch, working
around incomplete annotation, and validating that the reference you built
is behaving before you spend cluster hours on it.

## What you need before you start

| Requirement | Notes |
|-------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Cell Ranger ARC | Version pinned in each chapter |
| Genome FASTA | GRCz11 for the worked example; pin the release |
| Transcript annotation | Lawson Lab GTF, built against a specific Ensembl release |
| Compute | `mkref` and `count` are memory-hungry; per-step figures are given where relevant |
| Raw data | Paired GEX and ATAC FASTQs from the same library |

Mixing an annotation built against one Ensembl release with a FASTA from
another is a silent failure mode rather than an error. Chapter 1 covers
how to check.

## Chapters

1.  **Introduction** — the assay, why non-model organisms are harder, and
    what specifically goes wrong with zebrafish annotation.
2.  **Preprocessing** — building the reference and running Cell Ranger
    ARC.

Additional chapters are in progress. Read in order; each assumes the
decisions made before it.

## Conventions

::: callout-note
Notes flag context that is useful but not required to follow the steps.
:::

::: callout-warning
Warnings flag the failure modes that produce plausible-looking but wrong
output. These are the ones worth reading carefully.
:::

Shell commands are shown in full with real paths from the worked example.
Substitute your own rather than copying verbatim.

## Reproducibility and feedback

Chapters containing long-running steps are cached with Quarto's `freeze`,
so rebuilding the site does not re-execute Cell Ranger. Software versions
are stated per chapter.

Corrections and questions are welcome as issues on the
[source repository](https://github.com/Dartmouth-Data-Analytics-Core/zebrafish-multiome-vignette).
